source.title: Multilayer Lookahead: a Nested Version of Lookahead

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own optimizer comparisons and argues that multilayer Lookahead amplifies SGD's implicit regularization, but the reported results do not test the mapped conditions or measures as those claim versions specify. Its evidence is about changing the optimizer wrapper and comparing training and test performance.
record.gate_note: Reports CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training/test accuracy comparisons for SGD, Lookahead and Multilayer Lookahead; these bear on optimizer effects but do not directly test V4's adaptive-optimizer comparison. It also reports GAN Inception Score, which is outside the listed versions. Cited prior findings about batch size and generalization are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests nested Lookahead optimizers, but none of V1–V8. Classification compares momentum SGD with wrappers around momentum SGD, not adaptive methods against SGD (V4). Batch size is fixed at 50 (V5), and the implicit-regularizer analysis does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps (V7). References to small-batch generalization are prior findings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they argue that nested Lookahead amplifies SGD's implicit regularization, improves classification performance and reaches useful accuracy sooner. Their regularizer comparison assumes appropriately scaled learning rates; they explicitly cannot draw the same conclusion at equal learning rates. Their overall empirical claim also needs the Table 2 qualification that CIFAR-100 LA-2 finishes below SGD.
record.recipe_differences: Recursively wraps Lookahead around an inner optimizer; the paper compares optimizer variants and analyzes implicit regularization, rather than testing the catalog's memorization, architecture, batch-size, dropout, sharpness or example-removal claims.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and selected learning rate/configuration affect the reported comparison: on CIFAR-100 LA-2 scores below SGD, while LA-1, LA-3 and LA-4 score slightly above it; authors report the best learning rate differs between SGD and Multilayer Lookahead for CIFAR-100. They describe CIFAR-10 test gains with equal learning rates and both train and test accuracy improving.

fits_no_version.finding: Nested Lookahead produces small final test-accuracy gains on CIFAR-10; CIFAR-100 results depend on configuration, with LA-2 below SGD and LA-4 above it. All classification optimizers use momentum SGD as their base.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Wrapping momentum SGD in nested Lookahead can improve image-classification accuracy and early training performance, depending on dataset and configuration.

fits_no_version.finding: The modified-flow analysis attributes improved generalization to stronger alignment of gradients across minibatches under appropriately scaled learning rates; it does not test perturbation-based sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nested Lookahead strengthens an implicit gradient-alignment regularizer when learning rates are scaled to equalize progress per epoch.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix B.2 reports improved MNIST GAN Inception Scores using nested Lookahead around Adam, without an SGD comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nested Lookahead can improve generated-image quality relative to Adam and single-layer Lookahead in the tested MNIST GAN setup.

record.problems: The classification comparisons use a moderate parameter grid and the authors do not claim the selected configurations are near-optimal. Table results are averaged across 3 runs, but the text does not state a formal significance test. The reported accuracy values do not quantify a training-test error gap; exact training metrics are only referenced in Appendix B.1 plots.
record.rows_left_out: The text also reports training plots for CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 in Figures 1–3 and GAN Inception Score in Figure 5. No numerical values can be recovered from the supplied prose for those figures, and GAN Inception Score does not match a listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out classification or language performance, including tuning and recovery conditions.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that change the penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Removing highly memorized training examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Tables 1–2 report final comparisons averaged over three runs, following configuration selection described in Appendix B.1. The reported uncertainty is not identified as a standard deviation or standard error. No listed version has an unrecorded qualifying result.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited tuning; the image classification experiments use SGD with momentum for each optimizer, while the GAN uses Adam but reports Inception Score rather than held-out classification performance.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
